children: According to CNBC, Democratic groups and voting-rights advocates are seeking to join a federal lawsuit over the Justice Department’s effort to stop Alaska from certifying its U.S. Senate election results if Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan loses. The lawsuit, filed Oct. 22, seeks an order blocking certification in that scenario. The groups include Mary Peltola’s campaign, the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee, the League of Women Voters of Alaska and Common Cause. They argue that the federal government lacks authority to dictate candidate eligibility or ballot design, and that the Justice Department has offered no method for determining whether voters who selected another candidate named Daniel J. Sullivan intended to vote for the incumbent. The Democratic groups seek defendant-intervenor status so they can move to dismiss the case; the League and Common Cause have separately asked to join as defendants.

title: Democrats, Voting-Rights Groups Seek to Join Lawsuit Challenging Trump’s Bid to Block Alaska Senate Certification
